location.basis: CIA catalog address 125 Walnut Street matched to Old Original Bookbinder's, Wikidata Q7084674. P625 is a representative locator point, not a surveyed building outline. This is separate from Bookbinders at 215 South 15th Street.

CIA restaurant fields explicitly identify Bellevue-Stratford or a restaurant within that hotel. The six NYPL records have supplied printed-scan audits naming the Bellevue-Stratford in Philadelphia, all dated after the present hotel opened in 1904. National Register record 77001182 confirms the historical 200 S. Broad address. Wikidata Q7716429 P625 supplies a representative hotel point; it does not identify an individual dining room. Earlier Bellevue venues and sponsoring organizations are not assigned this point. CIA Palm record 19268 explicitly supplies 200 South Broad. It uses the same representative building point; its date remains unknown and no restaurant continuity or opening date is inferred.

The supplied printed-scan audit for NYPL 27260 names the Warwick in Philadelphia and gives 1701 Locust Street, dated May 12, 1959. NPS National Register record 78002460 independently identifies The Warwick at 1701 Locust Street, with significant years 1925 and 1928. Wikidata Q7773621 P625 supplies the representative building point, not a dining-room position.

The supplied printed-scan audits for NYPL 29996 (1948) and 30777 (1934) explicitly identify the Philadelphia Benjamin Franklin Hotel at 834 Chestnut Street. NPS National Register record 82003808 identifies the historical hotel at 822–840 Chestnut Street with significant year 1925. Wikidata Q4885674 P625 supplies a representative hotel point. The Poe House drawing at 530 North Seventh Street on 30777 is not the dinner venue; no point is assigned there.
